reason: The text passage from Exodus 3-4 contains only three named characters who actively participate in the narrative: (1) Moses (מֹשֶׁה), who is called and commissioned as a leader to guide the Israelites; (2) Aaron (אַהֲרֹן), who becomes Moses's co-leader and spokesman; and (3) YHWH (יְהוָה), the divine authority. While Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob are mentioned by name, they appear only as historical references to past figures, not as active characters. All three active named characters hold leadership roles or ultimate authority.
